skill.name: tdd-orchestrator
skill.description: Coordinate test-driven development with red-green-refactor workflows, test strategy guidance, quality gates, and multi-agent planning.
skill.summary: A practical guide for planning, coordinating, and improving test-driven development workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to maintain test-first discipline across features, services, and contributors. This skill organizes red-green-refactor work, testing layers, quality gates, and improvement activities.
actual_capabilities: Plan red-green-refactor cycles for new features and refactoring work.
Design balanced unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end testing strategies.
Coordinate parallel testing tasks across specialized agents and development streams.
Recommend test data, fixtures, mocks, stubs, and service virtualization approaches.
Define TDD metrics, quality gates, coverage thresholds, and feedback improvements.
limitations: It provides guidance and planning rather than executing tests or changing repositories.
It cannot verify framework behavior, build configuration, or environment-specific assumptions.
Recommendations may require adaptation to the project language, architecture, and team skills.
It does not replace security review, performance testing, or expert engineering judgment.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Break a feature into testable behaviors and define a practical red-green-refactor sequence with suitable test levels.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Testing Agents
use_cases.description: Create responsibilities, dependencies, and handoffs for unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end testing agents.

use_cases.title: Improve a Legacy System
use_cases.description: Build a characterization testing plan, establish safety nets, and sequence incremental refactoring for an existing codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a red-green-refactor workflow for this feature: [feature]. List the first behaviors to test and the expected implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Test Levels
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature description: [description]. Recommend unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end coverage, with a reason for each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Test Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent TDD workflow for [project]. Assign unit, integration, and end-to-end tasks, identify dependencies, and define handoff evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize Legacy Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incremental TDD refactoring plan for [system]. Include characterization tests, risk controls, test data isolation, quality gates, and rollback checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Plan TDD for a password reset feature.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering invalid requests, token issuance, token expiry, successful reset, and confirmation messaging. Each stage identifies the smallest test, implementation change, and refactoring checkpoint.

output_examples.input: Recommend a testing strategy for a service with an HTTP API and database.
output: Unit tests for validation and domain rules.
Integration tests for database transactions and persistence.
Contract tests for stable API behavior.
A small end-to-end suite for the highest-value user journeys.

output_examples.input: Organize parallel agents for a microservices TDD effort.
output_examples.output: A dependency-aware work plan assigns service-level tests, API contract checks, integration environments, and cross-service scenarios. Completion evidence includes test results, changed assumptions, and unresolved risks.

best_practices: Start with observable behavior and the smallest failing test.
Keep test layers balanced and isolate dependencies where practical.
Require test results and explicit assumptions before accepting workflow handoffs.
anti_patterns: Do not maximize coverage numbers without checking test behavior and value.
Do not use end-to-end tests for every rule that a unit test can verify.
Do not parallelize dependent work without clear ownership, contracts, and integration checkpoints.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and coordinate TDD practices, testing strategies, agent workflows, quality gates, and refactoring safety nets.

faq.question: Can it run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It produces guidance and plans. Your development tools and CI system must execute and verify the tests.

faq.question: Which testing levels does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, property-based, mutation, performance, and security-focused testing strategies.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose characterization tests, incremental safety nets, dependency isolation, and staged refactoring plans.

faq.question: Does it support multiple programming languages?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers Java, C#, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Go, with common testing frameworks and build tools.

faq.question: What should I provide in a prompt?
faq.answer: Provide the feature or system goal, technology stack, current tests, constraints, success criteria, and any known risks.
